ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within square $ABCD$, point $E$ is on side $BC$, and $AB = 3BE$. Draw $BF\perp AE$ through point $B$, intersecting with side $CD$ at point $F$. With $C$ as the center and $CF$ as the radius, draw a circle intersecting side $BC$ at point $G$. Connect $DG$, intersecting $BF$ at point $H$. What is the ratio of $DH$ to $HG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect AH and CH. Let AE and BF intersect at M,\\
$\because BF \perp AE$,\\
$\therefore \angle AMB = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAM + \angle ABM = 90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
$\therefore AB = BC = CD = AD$, $\angle ABE = \angle BCF = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABM + \angle CBF = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAE = \angle CBF$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABE \cong \triangle BCF$ (ASA),\\
$\therefore BE = CF$,\\
$\therefore BF = DF$,\\
$\because CG = CF$, $\angle DCG = \angle BCF$, DC = BC,\\
$\therefore \triangle BCF \cong \triangle DCG$ (SAS),\\
$\therefore \angle CBF = \angle CDG$,\\
Also, $\because \angle BHG = \angle DHF$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BHG \cong \triangle DHF$ (AAS),\\
$\therefore HG = HF$,\\
Also, $\because HC = HC$, CG = CF,\\
$\therefore \triangle HCG \cong \triangle HCF$ (SSS),\\
$\therefore \angle HCG = \angle HCF = 45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ Points A, H, and C are collinear,\\
$\because AD \parallel CG$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ADH \sim \triangle CGH$,\\
$\therefore \frac{DH}{HG} = \frac{AD}{CG} = \frac{AD}{BE} = \frac{AB}{BE} = \boxed{3\colon 1}$,\\

In △ABE and △BCF, ∠ABE=∠BCF=90°, AB=BC, and ∠BAE=∠CBF, so △ABE≅△BCF. Therefore BE=CF. Also because the center of the circle is C, the radius is CF, and the circle intersects BC at G, CG=CF=BE. Next compare △BCF and △DCG: BC=CD, CF=CG, and ∠BCF=∠DCG=90°, so △BCF≅△DCG. Therefore ∠CBF=∠CDG. Since BC=CD and CG=CF, it can be obtained that BG=BC-CG, DF=CD-CF, so BG=DF. Also because B, H, F are collinear, and D, H, G are collinear, ∠GBH=∠CBF and ∠HDF=∠CDG, hence ∠GBH=∠HDF; at the same time ∠BHG=∠DHF are vertical angles. Therefore △BHG≅△DHF, obtaining HG=HF. Now in △HCG and △HCF, HC is a common side, CG=CF, and HG=HF, so △HCG≅△HCF. Therefore CH bisects ∠GCF. Since CG is horizontally leftward along the bottom side of the square, and CF is vertically upward along the right side of the square, ∠GCF=90°, so CH is a 45° direction line, that is, H lies on the diagonal AC of the square. Because AD∥CG, and A, H, C are collinear, D, H, G are collinear, △ADH∼△CGH. Thus DH/HG=AD/CG. Also AD=AB, CG=CF=BE, and the problem states AB=3BE, so DH/HG=AD/CG=AB/BE=3/1. Therefore DH:HG=3:1.
